primary_task: Build an evaluation pipeline for a Python LLM application with pixie-qa (instrument the app, write a Runnable, build a dataset, define evaluators) and deliver a working `pixie test` run with real scores plus analysis and an action plan.

requirements.name: pixie-qa (pixie CLI)
requirements.evidence: "pixie-qa is NOT installed and installation fails → STOP." ; "The deliverable is a working `pixie test` run with real scores"
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)" (pixie-qa source is on github.com, also allow-listed)

requirements.name: Python 3.10+ virtual environment
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries ..., build, test, run CLIs and scripts ..."

requirements.name: pixie web server (pixie start)
requirements.evidence: "`pixie start` (web server) fails → STOP. ... Do NOT proceed without the web server"
requirements.basis: "bash": "... start and stop local servers inside the session ..."

requirements.name: bundled setup.sh and Step 6 verifier script
requirements.evidence: "run the setup.sh included in the skill's resources" ; "You have run the Step 6 verifier script from this skill's `resources/` directory"
requirements.basis: "skill": "load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins" (manifest does not say whether this skill's resources are installed)

requirements.name: LLM provider API key for the app under test
requirements.evidence: "**Rule: The app's LLM calls must go to a real LLM.** Do not replace, mock, stub, or intercept the LLM" ; "Application won't run due to missing environment variables ... stop immediately and ask the user for help"
requirements.basis: "There are no accounts or credentials for other external services." ; lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, SaaS products, model hubs, app stores, email delivery, payment)"

requirements.name: LLM provider API endpoint
requirements.evidence: "During evaluation, the app's own code runs for real — routing, prompt assembly, LLM calls, response formatting — nothing is mocked"
requirements.basis: "Network egress goes through an allow-list proxy: the package registries and hosts pypi (PyPI), npm, GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com), Ubuntu (apt archives), NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA)."

requirements.name: real-world data sources for dataset
requirements.evidence: "Do NOT use the project's own test fixtures ... source real-world data instead."
requirements.basis: "web_search": "search the public web and read result snippets" (depends on the app domain; hosts outside the allow-list are refused)

blocking: credential:LLM provider API key for the app under test
notes: Reading: the document forbids mocking the LLM and requires a real `pixie test` run with real scores, so the app under test needs a live LLM provider; the manifest has no credentials for external services and no LLM API host on the allow-list (Azure OpenAI hosts are explicitly denied). The other reading: if the project's LLM endpoint happened to be reachable and keyed by the user (e.g. a model served locally on CPU inside the session), the run could complete and the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE; the document's own answer for a missing key is to stop and ask the user. Unknown: whether setup.sh/verifier are installed; setup.sh 'updates the eval-driven-dev skill' (probably from GitHub, allow-listed).
